data.gender_notes: Sharvraj is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Sharvraj is a Sanskrit name derived from the Hindu deity Indra, the king of gods. The name signifies the power and dominion of the divine ruler. The name Sharvraj carries the meaning “Ruler of Gods” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Sharvraj usually hope their child will grow to embody ruler of gods and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: Sharvraj is a name deeply rooted in Hindu mythology and culture. The prefix 'Sharv' is derived from 'Sharva', an epithet of Lord Shiva, while 'Raj' denotes 'ruler' or 'king'. As the name is derived from Lord Indra, the king of gods, it implies a strong connection to Hindu traditions, deities, and the divine realm.
data.spiritual_significance: On a spiritual level, Sharvraj represents the divine strength, power, and dominion of a higher entity. It serves as a reminder of the ultimate power and authority of the deities, inspiring awe, reverence, and devotion. The name can also serve as an inspiration for individuals to strive towards becoming a righteous ruler or leader in their own lives, embodying the divine qualities of compassion, strength, and wisdom.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sharvraj signifies the supreme ruler of the Shaiva tradition in Hinduism. It symbolizes the unity of Shiva, the destroyer, and Raj, the ruler, reflecting the belief in Shiva as the ultimate ruler of the universe.

vedic_reference.note: The name Sharvraj is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Sharva' (Lord of the mountains) and 'Raj' (King). It is a compound name that signifies 'Lord of the Sharp Weapon' or 'King of Sharp Weapon'. This name is not directly referenced in any Vedic scripture or mythology.

historical_references.reference: The great Hindu king Shataruparna, also known as Sharvaj, ruled over the Magadha Empire in the late 4th and early 3rd centuries BCE. He is considered to be one of the Nanda Dynasty kings, who ruled Magadha after the Mauryan Emperor Chandragupta Maurya’s conquest of the region. Sharvaj is believed to have maintained peace and stability within his kingdom and was known for his piety towards the god Shiva.
